beats.say: A document from the internet first opens in Protected View, read only. That is your shield.
If a blank page shows text like this, stop. A real document does not ask you to press buttons.

title.text: Protected View: this file came from the internet

body.text: The document is blank, only a picture shows:
"To see the text, click Enable Editing, then Enable Content."

beats.say: A macro is a hidden command inside a document. It can install malware on the computer.
Also never accept an offer to download a special viewer from a website to open a document.

scenes.title: Opening a document
scenes.intro: You opened an attachment called tender terms. Read each window and decide at every step.

title.text: Protected View: this file came from the internet

body.text: The document is blank, only a picture shows:
"To see the text, click Enable Editing, then Enable Content."

steps.say: The document is blank and wants a click.

actions.label: Enable Editing
actions.feedback: You left Protected View. That mode exists to guard against files like this.

actions.label: Close the document
actions.feedback: Right. A blank page asking for a click is a trap.

actions.label: Report to IT security
actions.feedback: Great. You reported it without enabling editing.

body.text: Macros in this document are blocked because the file came from the internet.
The document says: "Unblock the file in its properties and allow macros."

steps.say: The app blocked the macros. The document asks you to unblock them.

actions.label: Unblock and allow macros
actions.feedback: The hidden macro ran and installed malware. Disconnect and call IT security now.

actions.label: Close the document
actions.feedback: You stopped in time. The app protected you and you did not bypass it.

body.text: Malicious "tender terms" documents are spreading. If you got one, report it.

actions.label: Report the email
actions.feedback: Right. Your report helps IT remove the email from every mailbox.

actions.label: Ignore
actions.feedback: You closed the file, but the email is still there. Report it so colleagues do not open it.

scenes.title: Fake PDF viewer
scenes.intro: A link in an email offers a program to open the document. What do you do?

steps.label: Update Sənəd Oxu to view this document

actions.label: Download and install
actions.feedback: The fake viewer is malware. Your browser can open PDF files by itself.

actions.label: Close tab
actions.feedback: Right. Programs are installed only by IT or your organisation's software centre.

actions.label: Report site
actions.feedback: Great. Reporting the site protects your colleagues too.

steps.say: A download started by itself. Check the file type.

actions.label: Open
actions.feedback: This is a program from a fake site. Opening it infects the computer.

actions.label: Delete
actions.feedback: Right. Delete a download you did not ask for without opening it.

actions.label: Report to IT
actions.feedback: Great. IT can block this site for everyone.

actions.label: Open document
actions.feedback: Right. Internal portal, the file opens in the browser, nothing to install.

actions.label: Report site
actions.feedback: This is your organisation's own portal and it asks for no install. Save reports for suspicious cases.

scenes.prompt: Find the signs of a trap in this email.

body.text: The document was made in an older format.
To view it, enable editing first, then enable content.
If it does not open, update your viewer here:

spots.label: Different domain
spots.explain: It uses the signing service name, but the domain is different. Report it.

spots.label: Request to enable
spots.explain: A real document can be read without enabling editing or macros.

spots.label: Macro file
spots.explain: An Office file ending in "m" (xlsm, docm) can carry macros.

spots.label: Program download link
spots.explain: Needing a special program for a document is a sign of a fake viewer.

scenes.prompt: A document asks for macros. Put the steps in order.

items.label: Report the email to IT security
If expected, ask the sender on a number you know

scenes.explain: First stop and close, then report. Check with the sender only on a number you already know.

points: A blank document asking for a click is a trap
Do not enable editing or macros: close and report
Never download a program from a site to open a document
